title: 3DGS-HPC: Distractor-free 3D Gaussian Splatting with Hybrid Patch-wise Classification
claim: Prior methods produce masks that miss transient distractors and leave rendering artifacts; ours yields cleaner masks and artifact-free renders.
layout: 4x6 image grid; rows are methods, columns are inputs and renders; yellow boxes
description: A grid of photographs with four rows, one per method: 3DGS, WildGaussians, SLS-mlp and HPC (Ours). The first four columns show Training views #1 to #4 of an outdoor scene with a wooden lounger and mountains. Row one shows the raw images, with a pedestrian, a tree trunk and shadows. The other rows show the images faded, with black overlays marking the pixels each method classifies as transient. WildGaussians and SLS-mlp masks are noisy, covering the sky and missing parts of the person. HPC masks are blocky and patch-based, and they cover the pedestrian cleanly. The last two columns show Rendered #1 and #2, with yellow boxes around artifact regions. Baseline renders show blur and ghosting there. The HPC renders are clean. The eye goes to the yellow boxes and the bottom row.
caption: Comparison between previous methods and our proposed Hybrid Patch-wise Classification (HPC). When training 3DGS with static scenes disturbed by transient distractors, previous methods utilize image semantic priors but fail to separate transient distractors (\eg, pedestrians and shadows) from static backgrounds (\eg, mountains). By addressing their inherent semantic limitations, our method can generate binary masks that better represent transient distractors, thereby removing related artifacts in rendered results (yellow boxes).
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has demonstrated remarkable performance in novel view synthesis and 3D scene reconstruction, but its quality often degrades in real-world environments due to transient distractors, such as moving objects and varying shadows. Existing methods commonly introduce semantic priors from pre-trained vision models either to group pixels into coherent regions or to define perceptual error metrics. However, semantic grouping is often misaligned with the binary static/transient distinction, while perceptual features can be fragile under appearance perturbations introduced during 3DGS optimization. We propose 3DGS-HPC, a framework that addresses these issues by combining two complementary principles: a patch-wise classification strategy that leverages local spatial consistency for robust region-level decisions, and a hybrid classification metric that adaptively integrates photometric and perceptual cues for more reliable separation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority and robustness of our method in mitigating distractors to improve 3DGS-based novel view synthesis. Our project page is https://cnhaox.github.io/3DGS-HPC/ .
